headline: Senate resolution to overturn an immigration court rule on Board of Immigration Appeals procedures failed to advance.
what_it_does: This resolution would have used the Congressional Review Act to cancel a rule from the Executive Office for Immigration Review about how the Board of Immigration Appeals handles appeals. The Board is the body that reviews decisions made by immigration judges. If adopted, the rule would have had no force, and the agency could not issue a substantially similar rule without new approval from Congress. No official summary is available, so the specific changes the rule made are not described here.

who_it_affects.how: The rules for how their appeals are handled by the Board of Immigration Appeals would have stayed as they were before this rule.
They would have continued following the earlier appeal procedures instead of the new rule's procedures.
The agency would have been blocked from using this rule or issuing a substantially similar one without Congress's approval.
